methods.label: Use the percentage relationship
methods.explanation:
15 is \(30\%\) of 50. Since \(30\%=\frac{30}{100}\), this means \(15\div50=\frac{30}{100}\). Multiplying the quotient by \(100\) gives
\[
15\div50\times100=\frac{30}{100}\times100=30.
\]
methods.levelReason: The percentage relationship, conversion to a fraction, and multiplication of a fraction by an integer are within Grade 6 scope.

methods.label: Compute the decimal quotient, then multiply by 100
methods.explanation:
Multiplication and division have equal priority, so evaluate from left to right. First \(15\div50=0.3\). Multiplying by \(100\) moves the decimal point two places to the right, so
\[
15\div50\times100=0.3\times100=30.
\]
methods.levelReason: This direct arithmetic route uses Grade 5 decimal division and Grade 4 decimal scaling. The recorded p112 assessment covers only the operation-order interpretation.
